$about: Observations for the 2026-08-03 round, backfilled on 2026-08-04 from research/testing-log-2026-08-03.md. Every 'fix' link was independently re-verified via `gh pr view <n> -R repository-standards/core --json number,title,state,mergedAt,body` on 2026-08-04, not copied from the log. PR #10 is confirmed CLOSED (not merged) per the log's own account. One observation (case STACK-01) is a real, verified mismatch: the log attributes its fix to PR #1, but PR #1's actual diff does not contain it - see the evidence field and the codify report. On 2026-08-05, every observation in this file that had verdict "fail" with a non-empty "fix" field was independently re-run against the current, fully-merged tree (not re-read from the PR) - the fixed-defect-keeps-its-fail convention this suite started with was itself a defect: a fixed bug should read as fixed. Verdicts that held were flipped to "pass" with the fix field kept as provenance; one (DOC-01) did not fully hold and stays "fail" with a corrected evidence field.

$elicitation.$why: This corpus measures whether the tooling conforms - gates, manifests, drift counts. No person was prompted in any of these runs and none was meant to be, so it evidences nothing about whether the standard asks anybody anything. It was never labelled that way, which is how 377 green observations came to read as validation of a product whose central promise is being guided.

Re-verified 2026-08-05, live. Scripted the case's own procedure (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A` per manifest path, VERSION at that commit, compared to the entry's `since`) across all 47 `files` entries. The original defect (a blind version-bump string-replace stamping the CURRENT version across every matching entry) does not reproduce - `since` values are heterogeneous (0.1.0 x4, 0.2.0, 0.3.0 x3, 0.4.0 x2, 0.7.2 x2, 0.8.0 x32, 0.8.14 x1, unreleased x2), not a uniform block. Most entries read `since: 0.8.0` because that is genuinely when the manifest-tracked shape of the tree began (the pre-1.0 `core/` -> `dist/` restructuring predates the manifest schema this case checks against), not because of corruption - `git log --follow` across that reorg's renames disagrees with 0.8.0 for most of these paths, but chasing pre-manifest history is not what `since` is declaring. One genuine, current anomaly found instead: the `scripts/lib` entry declares `since: "0.8.14"`, a version that does not exist yet - VERSION is still 0.8.13 and no release has been cut. Every other not-yet-released entry in this same manifest (CHANGELOG.md, scripts/decision-records-check.mjs) correctly uses the literal string "unreleased" instead of guessing a future number; scripts/lib does not follow that convention (added by a later commit, b2bd46b, unrelated to the PR that fixed this case). `since` values are supposed to reflect real history, and a value ahead of the current VERSION cannot, by construction, match any real commit. Left as fail rather than flipped to pass: the core defect this case targeted does not recur, but its promise ("every value matches real history") does not fully hold today because of this one entry.
